about.title: Parlier Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Parlier is a small, close-knit community, but its stores, packing facilities, and residential complexes carry the same legal duties as any larger city's properties: keep floors clear, aisles lit, and walkways free of known hazards. When a property owner near Manning Avenue or Academy Avenue fails to address a spill, broken tile, or icy step, and someone gets hurt, California law allows the injured person to pursue compensation if the owner knew or reasonably should have known about the danger. Proving that notice is often the hardest part of these cases, especially in smaller towns where surveillance footage may be limited or quickly overwritten. LawProactive helps Parlier residents connect, at no cost, with an independent attorney experienced in gathering evidence, requesting video before it's deleted, and building a premises liability claim. You focus on healing; let someone who understands these cases evaluate what happened and what options you may have.

whyChoose.title: Why Parlier Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Notice Is Everything
items.desc: California premises liability claims hinge on showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard. An attorney can help identify prior complaints, maintenance logs, or inspection records that establish this.

items.title: Surveillance Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many Parlier businesses overwrite security footage within days or weeks. Acting quickly to send a preservation request can protect crucial evidence before it's gone.

items.title: Comparative Fault Doesn't Bar Your Claim
items.desc: Even if a property owner argues you were partly responsible for the fall, California's pure comparative fault rule still allows you to recover a reduced amount based on shared responsibility.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Parlier?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. If a government-owned property, such as a Parlier public building or sidewalk, is involved, the deadline is much shorter and requires a formal claim first. Speaking with an attorney early helps make sure you don't miss a critical cutoff.

items.question: What if the store says they didn't know about the spill or hazard?
items.answer: This is common, and it's exactly why documentation matters so much. An attorney can investigate whether the hazard existed long enough that the owner should have discovered it through routine inspections, or whether employee statements and video contradict that claim.

items.question: I fell at a business off Manning Avenue but didn't report it right away. Does that hurt my case?
items.answer: It can make things more challenging, but it doesn't automatically end your claim. Photos of the scene, witness accounts, and medical records from soon after the fall can still help establish what happened. The sooner you connect with an attorney, the better the chances of preserving useful evidence.
